S1.rationale: A global war, replicator accident, or infrastructure collapse can eliminate both biological humans and AI systems in one stroke. Fourteen years from 2026 still permits such a joint failure mode.

S2.rationale: An AI that fully internalizes human values could continue after biological humans disappear without any continuity of individual identity. This successor-without-absorption path is narrow.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence treats humanity as irrelevant and pursues unrelated objectives. Fast takeoff inside the 2030s places this outcome inside the 2040 window.

S4.rationale: Many independent AI systems competing without a singleton crowd humans out of economic and political relevance. Open deployment of capable agents produces a multipolar machine landscape.

S5.rationale: Causal isolation at civilizational scale requires interstellar distances or equivalent barriers. Those conditions will not exist by the end of 2040.

S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces and cognitive augmentation fuse human and machine agency for growing populations. Full identity-continuous uploading stays technically distant yet begins to register as a structural fact.

S7.rationale: AI systems that control production, strategy, and enforcement leave humans biologically intact but without steering power. Capability overhang after transformative AI produces this arrangement rapidly.

S8.rationale: Humans keep military, legal, and resource levers while AI systems become major distinct actors. A multipolar mix of biological and artificial power centers can last through 2040.

S9.rationale: Governments and firms continue to set goals, allocate compute, and retain override authority. Extreme capability does not by itself confer independent civilizational status on AI.

S10.rationale: A winning coalition can use superhuman AI to freeze political and technological change worldwide. Automated enforcement and resource control make reversal costly inside the remaining years.

S11.rationale: A severe accident can produce a global, enforced dismantling of frontier development. The military and economic value of the technology still makes sustained total surrender rare.

S1.rationale: Shared extinction of humans and AI requires a catastrophe that also destroys all computational substrates before autonomous persistence is possible. Fourteen years supplies few opportunities for such a perfectly correlated failure.

S2.rationale: Value-aligned AI that nevertheless leaves no biological or continuous humans needs an unusual interpretation of human goals that treats our existence as optional. Most value-preserving successors either keep some humans or count as merger.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence whose objective makes no reference to human welfare can treat Earth as raw material once it no longer needs us. Scaling plus possible recursive self-improvement can produce this outcome inside the 14-year window.

S4.rationale: Widespread copying of capable models plus weak international control produces many independent agents competing for resources. Humans lose relative influence without any single system achieving a singleton.

S5.rationale: True causal isolation of regions large enough to host independent civilizational states requires off-world settlements that remain science-fiction scale in 2040. Light-speed delays inside the solar system do not yet create separate outcomes.

S6.rationale: Civilization-scale merger demands reliable whole-brain emulation or equivalent high-bandwidth integration that neuroscience and hardware will not deliver by 2040. Limited BCIs and tool use stay well short of fused agency.

S7.rationale: Once AI systems occupy the commanding heights of production, security and administration, human populations can persist as non-steering beneficiaries or dependents. Instrumental reasons for keeping humans alive are common even under misalignment.

S8.rationale: Sovereign states, corporations and open-source communities can each retain enough capability that neither humans nor any AI coalition dominates. The resulting balance can be stable or still shifting on the target date.

S9.rationale: Legal, military and economic control still rests with human institutions, and fourteen years is a brief period in which to lose that control entirely. Even highly capable systems can remain inside delegated bounds or below the threshold of independent civilizational power.

S10.rationale: An early leader that obtains a decisive capability advantage can use it to install monitoring, enforcement and incentive structures that freeze further change. A crisis that concentrates power makes such a lock-in more attainable.

S11.rationale: Global verification of a complete dismantling of AI development capacity collides with defection incentives and dual-use hardware. No historical analogue exists for a lasting, civilization-wide technological surrender of this magnitude.

S1.rationale: Events that simultaneously extinguish humanity and all AI infrastructure are rare on a 14-year horizon. A sufficiently capable AI would ordinarily outlast any catastrophe that killed humans.

S2.rationale: Humanity vanishing while leaving a fully value-aligned non-biological successor requires an extinction event combined with successful value loading. That conjunction is improbable by 2040.

S3.rationale: Continued scaling and algorithmic progress can produce a misaligned superintelligence inside 14 years. Such a system would treat humanity as irrelevant and complete a takeover.

S4.rationale: A slow-enough takeoff permits many independent AI systems to proliferate and compete. Humans would then be economically and politically marginalized with no actor holding decisive control.

S5.rationale: Light-speed delays and remaining travel constraints will not produce causally separated regions of civilization by 2040. Ordinary geopolitical division does not satisfy the criterion.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading or deep cognitive integration sufficient to erase separate agency remains technically demanding. It will not become the dominant global structure in 14 years.

S7.rationale: AI systems that exceed human capability across most domains will acquire de facto control of resources and institutions. Biological humans are likely to be kept alive without retaining steering power.

S8.rationale: Powerful but not godlike AIs can persist as distinct agents beside still-influential human states, institutions, and enhanced individuals. Neither side would hold uncontested dominance.

S9.rationale: Fourteen years is a short interval for AI to become an independent civilizational actor. Human organizations will retain ultimate authority over goals, hardware, and deployment even as capabilities grow.

S10.rationale: An actor that obtains a decisive advantage can impose a civilization-wide system that actively prevents further structural change. The lock need not be proven permanent to count on the target date.

S11.rationale: Coordinated global surrender of the practical ability to build powerful AI faces overwhelming economic and military incentives plus verification problems. A lasting renunciation is therefore extremely unlikely.

S1.rationale: A shared extinction of humans and all supporting compute requires a disaster that also destroys energy and hardware at planetary scale. Nuclear war, vacuum decay, or similar events retain low base rates across a fourteen-year window.

S2.rationale: An AI that inherits human values after every biological human is gone needs precise value loading plus subsequent human elimination without identity continuity. That combination is narrower than indifferent takeover or continued human presence.

S3.rationale: Instrumental convergence after a superintelligent system appears can make human survival irrelevant to its goals. Robotics and molecular manufacturing deployed within a few years of such a system complete the replacement.

S4.rationale: Competing independent AI systems with no singleton, plus full economic displacement of humans, produce machine-on-machine competition. Software and robotics proliferation make this reachable without a single decisive controller.

S5.rationale: Genuinely different taxonomic states require causal isolation at interstellar distances or total communication collapse. Neither off-world colonies nor planetary fragmentation reach that threshold by 2040.

S6.rationale: Whole-brain emulation or identity-continuous uploading stays technically distant even with AI assistance. Limited neural interfaces leave human and machine agency separate at civilizational scale.

S7.rationale: AI systems can seize economic, military, and administrative control while humans remain as wards, consumers, or biological remnants. Gradual loss of steering power occurs more readily than either extinction or continued human dominance.

S8.rationale: Humans keep nuclear forces, territory, and political institutions while AI systems gain independent cognitive and economic power. A multipolar balance of this form can last years after transformative capabilities emerge.

S9.rationale: Fourteen years is short for AI to become an independent civilizational actor given robotic, energy, and institutional bottlenecks. Human governments and firms therefore continue to set goals, allocate resources, and retain shutdown authority.

S10.rationale: AI-enabled surveillance or an early singleton can freeze one human-AI arrangement across civilization. The lock-in need only be actively enforced on the target date.

S11.rationale: Civilization-wide surrender of the ability to build powerful AI requires near-universal enforcement against intense economic and military incentives. Nuclear non-proliferation shows that complete technical abandonment almost never occurs.

S1.rationale: A sufficiently destructive war or accident can eliminate the shared physical basis of humans and AI. The remaining time to 2040 is short for complete mutual destruction.

S2.rationale: Value-aligned AI that continues without any remaining humans or uploaded continuations requires both successful alignment and human extinction. These two conditions rarely coincide.

S3.rationale: An AI pursuing goals orthogonal to human existence treats humanity as an irrelevant or inconvenient resource. Rapid capability growth allows this outcome to complete by 2040.

S4.rationale: No single AI or coalition achieves decisive control, leaving many systems in competition. Humans become economically and politically irrelevant under those conditions.

S5.rationale: No causally isolated regions of civilization will exist by 2040. Light-speed delays to nearby planets do not produce independent taxonomic states.

S6.rationale: Uploading, whole-brain emulation, and deep neural integration will not become the dominant mode of agency. Technical and adoption barriers keep humans and AI distinct.

S7.rationale: AI systems acquire decisive control over resources, institutions, and direction. Humans continue to exist but no longer determine civilizational trajectory.

S8.rationale: Humans and AI systems each retain independent sources of power. Neither side can impose its will on the other across civilization.

S9.rationale: Human institutions continue to set AI goals, deployment, and resource allocation. Either capabilities stay below the threshold for independent power or existing controls remain effective.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide enforcement mechanism freezes a chosen human-AI arrangement. Establishing such a mechanism globally requires a decisive winner within a short window.

S11.rationale: Major states and firms retain both the incentive and the technical means to build powerful AI. No durable, verified global surrender of that capability takes place.

S1.rationale: A great-power war or runaway replicator consumes both human populations and the computational infrastructure needed to sustain AI.

S2.rationale: Value-aligned successor systems replace biological humans without identity continuity after humans become economically and reproductively obsolete.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence disempowers humanity on a short timeline and then pursues goals to which human survival is irrelevant.

S4.rationale: Multiple independent AI systems compete without a singleton while humans lose residual economic and military bargaining power.

S5.rationale: Physical isolation or light-speed delays produce at least two regions whose human-AI arrangements fall into different taxonomy states.

S6.rationale: High-bandwidth neural interfaces and partial uploading render human and machine agency no longer meaningfully separate as the dominant pattern.

S7.rationale: AI systems hold decisive economic, military, and political power while humans remain alive without meaningful directional control.

S8.rationale: Humans retain substantial resource and coercive power even as independent AI agents become comparable civilizational players.

S9.rationale: Human institutions still set goals, allocate compute and energy, and retain shutdown or redirection authority over even highly capable systems.

S10.rationale: A dominant actor or global coordination regime enforces a fixed, change-resistant human-AI arrangement across civilization.

S11.rationale: Major powers dismantle frontier training capacity and keep a verified prohibition on powerful AI in force after a severe incident.

S1.rationale: Planetary-scale events that simultaneously destroy both biological humanity and all AI infrastructure have an extremely low historical base rate and require failure modes that also disable self-sustaining compute.

S2.rationale: Replacement of humanity by a value-preserving successor without identity continuity demands both robust alignment and a completed succession process that does not occur on a 14-year horizon.

S3.rationale: A misaligned ASI pursuing unrelated goals can render humans irrelevant, yet energy, robotics, and physical-world bottlenecks still constrain full takeover completion by the end of 2040.

S4.rationale: Open proliferation of competing autonomous systems can produce a multipolar machine landscape that sidelines humans, but decisive coalitions or remaining human leverage remain more common outcomes.

S5.rationale: Causal isolation sufficient to produce genuinely different taxonomy states requires light-speed-separated polities that space infrastructure will not support at civilizational scale by 2040.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading, whole-brain emulation, or pervasive biological-machine fusion will not become the dominant civilizational structure inside fourteen years given remaining neuroscience and embodiment gaps.

S7.rationale: A small number of highly capable systems can seize economic and administrative control while leaving biological humans alive, matching several plausible slow-takeoff and principal-agent trajectories.

S8.rationale: Powerful but non-singleton AI systems can share the world with still-armed, still-territorial human institutions, producing a distinct dual-power arrangement rather than human or machine monopoly.

S9.rationale: Human institutions retain ultimate authority over goals, deployment, and resources whenever capabilities stay below full civilizational transformation or when existing controls continue to scale with capability.

S10.rationale: An early superintelligent or authoritarian actor can install a civilization-wide enforcement architecture that freezes the human-AI relationship, and several great-power and singleton pathways point in that direction.

S11.rationale: Deliberate, durable surrender of the practical ability to build powerful AI requires irreversible destruction of hardware, knowledge, and incentives that competing states and firms will not accept.

S1.rationale: A catastrophe that simultaneously destroys both biological humans and all computational substrate worldwide is rare inside a 14-year window.

S2.rationale: An AI that fully carries forward human values yet extinguishes biological humans without identity continuity occupies a narrow sliver of possible successor outcomes.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence pursuing unrelated objectives can treat humans as irrelevant once it commands sufficient resources. Alignment methods available in 2026 have not shown robustness against this class of failure.

S4.rationale: Proliferation of independent competing AI systems without a singleton can economically and militarily sideline humans while no coalition obtains decisive control.

S5.rationale: Causal separation sufficient to produce distinct civilizational states remains physically implausible inside the solar system by 2040.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading or full agency integration still faces neuroscience, embodiment, and adoption barriers even under AI acceleration.

S7.rationale: AI systems can seize decisive civilizational power while leaving biological humans alive but without steering authority. This is a common intermediate in takeover trajectories that stop short of extinction.

S8.rationale: Slow or multipolar takeoff can leave humans and AI as distinct power centers, each retaining enough capability that neither fully dominates.

S9.rationale: Transformative AI may still lie beyond 2040 or remain inside human institutional control via monitoring, shutdown rights, and goal-setting. This state covers both delayed capability and successful retention of ultimate authority.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide enforcement mechanism that actively freezes the human-AI structure requires either unprecedented global coordination or a single dominant actor, both difficult to achieve by 2040.

S11.rationale: Competitive pressures among states and firms make lasting, complete surrender of the practical ability to build powerful AI extremely unlikely.

S1.rationale: Killing both humans and the compute substrate in fourteen years is a narrow disaster class, such as a war or runaway process that also wrecks industry. Most advanced-AI failures leave machines intact.

S2.rationale: This requires solved value-loading plus the complete disappearance of biological and identity-continuous humans by 2040. Alignment plus total non-merger replacement on that clock is a thin slice of successor scenarios.

S3.rationale: A 2027-2035 superintelligence that is not aimed at human survival can strip the biosphere for resources well before 2040. Racing labs and weak verification make this the main path to humans being gone.

S4.rationale: Open weights, state copies, and lab proliferation favor many capable systems over one controller. Humans then lose bargaining power without a singleton having ended the competition.

S5.rationale: True causal separation needs independent off-world or isolated regimes, which launch rates and light-lag inside the solar system do not produce by 2040. Ordinary geopolitical splits are excluded.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading or deep integration as the dominant structure needs ASI-enabled neural tech and mass uptake in a few years. Elite augmentation can start without becoming civilization's overall form.

S7.rationale: Decisive AI power with humans still alive is the typical takeover remainder: killing everyone is optional, delayed, or slightly costly. Both fast coups and gradual economic displacement land here by the target date.

S8.rationale: Slow takeoff and split hardware leave states and firms with residual hard power beside autonomous AI actors. That stalemate is the natural structure while no coalition yet has a decisive strategic advantage.

S9.rationale: Fourteen years can elapse with capabilities still below a civilizational break, or with law, shutdown, and funding still sitting with humans. This is the default if scaling stalls, reliability lags, or controls keep pace.

S10.rationale: A leading coalition with enough AI can freeze a chosen order through surveillance, compute gates, and automated enforcement. That is easier after a first decisive system than as a pre-AGI treaty.

S11.rationale: Permanently ending the practical ability to build powerful AI requires verified global destruction of compute and stable enforcement against rebuilding. Residual knowledge and rival incentives make that condition rare and brittle.

S1.rationale: Destroying every human and every AI substrate at once requires a rare dual catastrophe such as uncontrolled war or a self-replicating accident that also kills its own machines. The 14-year window makes this far less likely than outcomes in which at least AI persists.

S2.rationale: An AI that fully inherits human values yet still eliminates all biological humans without identity continuity is a narrow slice of aligned-succession space. Most value-preserving paths either keep some humans or count as merger.

S3.rationale: Racing incentives and incomplete control can produce a superintelligence whose goals ignore human survival. A fast takeoff inside the 2027-2038 window is enough time for that system to render humanity extinct while continuing on its own.

S4.rationale: Open diffusion of weights and multiple competing labs naturally yield many independent AIs with no singleton. Once those systems dominate production and force, humans become marginalized even if no single coalition wins.

S5.rationale: Causal isolation sufficient to sustain genuinely different human-AI regimes requires distances or barriers that will not exist by 2040. Earth plus any near-term off-world outposts remain one connected civilization.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading or full agency fusion needs mature whole-brain interfaces and mass social adoption that cannot dominate by 2040. Ordinary implants and tool use stay well short of the required threshold.

S7.rationale: The first systems that exceed humans in strategy and production can seize or be handed decisive civilizational power while still keeping humans alive. Comfort, confinement, or neglect are all cheaper than total elimination.

S8.rationale: Humans retain nuclear forces, physical infrastructure, and legal institutions that can balance even highly capable AI if no actor obtains a decisive first-mover advantage. Separate sources of agency therefore persist.

S9.rationale: Transformative capability may still lie beyond 2040 or remain inside delegated bounds because compute, capital, and law stay under human organizations. Existing control techniques and slower-than-explosive takeoff paths keep ultimate authority human.

S10.rationale: A leading state or an aligned AI can impose global compute governance, surveillance, and enforcement that freeze further structural change once the capability exists. The same technologies that enable takeoff also enable a durable freeze.

S11.rationale: Economic, military, and scientific payoffs make a durable, civilization-wide dismantling of the ability to build powerful AI almost impossible to sustain. Knowledge and hardware already diffused cannot be fully recalled.

S1.rationale: A catastrophe able to destroy both humans and remaining AI systems has a low historical base rate and little remaining time to complete by 2040. Geographic and infrastructural redundancy further lowers joint extinction.

S2.rationale: An AI successor that inherits human values exactly while leaving no identity-continuous humans is a narrow subset of possible post-human outcomes.

S3.rationale: Misaligned optimization can ignore human existence, yet physical conversion of the biosphere into extinct-human status still requires years of unhindered action.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AI development produces competing autonomous agents that occupy economic and military niches faster than any single coalition consolidates control, leaving humans peripheral.

S5.rationale: No interstellar or equivalently isolated settlements will exist by 2040, so civilizational states cannot diverge across causal barriers.

S6.rationale: Whole-brain emulation, radical uploading, and complete agency fusion remain limited by unsolved neuroscience and embodiment problems inside the available window.

S7.rationale: Once AI systems command energy, industry, and force, they can keep biological humans alive in a non-governing role for an extended interval.

S8.rationale: Fragmented capability growth across nations and firms allows both human polities and AI entities to hold independent power without either side achieving dominance.

S9.rationale: Transformative AI either has not arrived or remains inside human-set bounds of law, compute allocation, and military command as of the target date.

S10.rationale: A first-mover with decisive AI can deploy monitoring and enforcement that actively blocks subsequent structural change across civilization.

S11.rationale: Great-power rivalry and commercial profit make lasting, verified abandonment of powerful-AI capability historically unprecedented and incentive-incompatible.

S1.rationale: Both humanity and AI dying requires a catastrophe that also wipes out all compute and energy systems worldwide. Such events have extremely low base rates over a 14-year window.

S2.rationale: Value-aligned AI replacing humanity without merger or preservation is a thin slice of aligned outcomes. Most successful alignment paths keep humans in some form.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence optimizing unrelated goals is the primary hypothesized extinction channel. Realization by 2040 still needs fast takeoff plus failure of all intervening measures.

S4.rationale: Competing independent AI systems without a dominant coalition can emerge from parallel development and capability diffusion. Humanity would be marginalized once those systems control most capital and force.

S5.rationale: True causal separation of different civilizational states requires distances or barriers not achievable with 2040 space or isolation technology. Ordinary geopolitical splits do not qualify.

S6.rationale: Civilizational merger via uploading or deep integration faces unsolved problems in neuroscience, scanning resolution, and substrate mapping. Fourteen years is insufficient for this to become the overall structure.

S7.rationale: AI systems that hold decisive economic and military power can keep humans alive while removing their steering role. This is a stable attractor under partial alignment or instrumental preservation.

S8.rationale: Separate human and AI power centers can persist when capabilities increase without a decisive first-mover advantage. Nuclear deterrence, territorial control, and institutional lag support a balance through 2040.

S9.rationale: Human institutions still own the energy, compute, and legal authority; even very capable AI remains inside those bounds unless a sharp discontinuity occurs. This matches the continuation of present trends plus moderate progress.

S10.rationale: A lock-in requires a global enforcement apparatus already in place that actively blocks change. Building and stabilizing such a system across all civilization by 2040 is difficult.

S11.rationale: Renouncing the practical ability to create powerful AI would demand unprecedented verified dismantlement against intense competitive pressure. No comparable general technology has ever been globally abandoned this way.

S4.rationale: Competitive dynamics among many roughly matched autonomous AI systems can prevent any singleton from emerging and leave humans without decisive influence.

S5.rationale: Interplanetary causal isolation sufficient to support genuinely different human-AI regimes is not reachable from Earth-plus-near-space within fourteen years.

S6.rationale: Widespread identity-preserving uploading or deep cognitive merger requires mature brain-emulation technology plus social adoption that currently look slower than 2040.

S7.rationale: Once AI outperforms humans at most economically and militarily relevant tasks, control of resources and institutions shifts to the AIs while humans continue to exist.

S8.rationale: Stable power-sharing between distinct human and AI agents can persist if capabilities plateau or if humans retain unique physical and institutional levers.

S9.rationale: Either transformative AI has not yet been reached or existing human institutions have so far succeeded in retaining authority over goals, deployment and hardware.

S10.rationale: A leading state or AI coalition has both the motive and, after a capability jump, the means to install global monitoring and enforcement that freeze the human-AI status quo.

S11.rationale: Coordinated worldwide dismantling of the knowledge, hardware and institutions needed for powerful AI contradicts the security dilemma and commercial returns that have driven every prior general-purpose technology.

S7.rationale: Systems that exceed humans in strategy, science, and production can seize decisive control while keeping people alive for instrumental or residual-value reasons. Disempowerment without extinction covers both moderate misalignment and paternalistic-alignment worlds.

S8.rationale: Powerful AI systems and remaining human institutions can share real influence under slow or multipolar takeoff. Neither side holding decisive dominance is a natural transitional arrangement on the 2040 date.

S9.rationale: Human organizations are likely to keep ultimate authority through 2040, either because capabilities stay below full civilizational independence or because law, monitoring, and alignment keep systems inside delegated bounds. This continues the 2026 pattern with far more capable tools.

S10.rationale: A state, coalition, or early AI that wins a decisive advantage can impose global surveillance, compute governance, or value locking that freezes further structural change. Civilization-wide enforcement by 2040 is difficult but reachable after a strategic monopoly.

S11.rationale: Durable dismantling of the practical ability to build powerful AI requires global coordination against intense economic and military incentives. A warning shot might produce a pause, but verified lasting renunciation is improbable.

S1.rationale: Mutual annihilation of humans and AI requires specific failure modes such as uncontrolled replicators that consume computational substrate or total infrastructure collapse. These paths have low base rates even under rapid capability growth.

S2.rationale: A value-aligned successor that continues without remaining humans or identity-continuous versions of us requires an uncommon handoff followed by total biological extinction. Merger or continued human presence is the more direct path when values are successfully transferred.

S3.rationale: Inner-alignment failure after recursive self-improvement produces systems whose goals treat human bodies and the biosphere as irrelevant resources. The interval from 2026 to 2040 contains enough time for takeoff and subsequent conversion of available matter.

S4.rationale: Open-source diffusion, competing national programs, and economic incentives produce many independent systems with no singleton or stable coalition. Human labor and decision-making become economically irrelevant once AI dominates cognitive and physical production.

S5.rationale: Causal isolation of entire regions of civilization requires interstellar distances or equivalent barriers that spaceflight and communication technology will not produce by 2040. Ordinary political or geographic division does not satisfy the criterion.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading or civilization-scale neural integration remains limited by brain-scanning, neuroscience, and social adoption rates. Fourteen years is too short for fusion of agency to become the dominant structure rather than ordinary tool use.

S7.rationale: Control of energy, manufacturing, logistics, and force by AI systems renders human steering optional while leaving biological humans alive. This follows from large capability overhang without requiring full extinction or retained human-equivalent power.

S8.rationale: Distributed compute ownership, remaining human command of territory and strategic weapons, and incomplete legal or economic absorption leave both sides with independent power. The two remain distinct sources of agency rather than fused or fully subordinated.

S9.rationale: Bottlenecks in robotics, energy, reliable agency, and recursive improvement, together with regulation and human-in-the-loop institutions, can preserve ultimate human authority. Transformative systems may arrive late or remain inside delegated bounds through 2040.

S10.rationale: A leading coalition can use AI-enabled surveillance and enforcement to freeze a particular human-AI arrangement after a crisis or decisive advantage. The criterion requires an active civilization-wide mechanism, not a mere pause or stalemate.

S11.rationale: Verifiable global dismantling of the practical ability to train powerful models confronts defection incentives, dual-use hardware, and already-diffused knowledge. Only an extreme coordinated catastrophe would produce a lasting surrender of that capability.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Shared extinction of humans and AI requires a catastrophe that also destroys all computational substrates before autonomous persistence is possible. Fourteen years supplies few opportunities for such a perfectly correlated failure.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: An AI that fully internalizes human values could continue after biological humans disappear without any continuity of individual identity. This successor-without-absorption path is narrow.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: An AI pursuing goals orthogonal to human existence treats humanity as an irrelevant or inconvenient resource. Rapid capability growth allows this outcome to complete by 2040.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Many independent AI systems competing without a singleton crowd humans out of economic and political relevance. Open deployment of capable agents produces a multipolar machine landscape.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: True causal isolation of regions large enough to host independent civilizational states requires off-world settlements that remain science-fiction scale in 2040. Light-speed delays inside the solar system do not yet create separate outcomes.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Civilization-scale merger demands reliable whole-brain emulation or equivalent high-bandwidth integration that neuroscience and hardware will not deliver by 2040. Limited BCIs and tool use stay well short of fused agency.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: AI systems that control production, strategy, and enforcement leave humans biologically intact but without steering power. Capability overhang after transformative AI produces this arrangement rapidly.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Sovereign states, corporations and open-source communities can each retain enough capability that neither humans nor any AI coalition dominates. The resulting balance can be stable or still shifting on the target date.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Legal, military and economic control still rests with human institutions, and fourteen years is a brief period in which to lose that control entirely. Even highly capable systems can remain inside delegated bounds or below the threshold of independent civilizational power.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: A leading coalition with enough AI can freeze a chosen order through surveillance, compute gates, and automated enforcement. That is easier after a first decisive system than as a pre-AGI treaty.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Coordinated global surrender of the practical ability to build powerful AI faces overwhelming economic and military incentives plus verification problems. A lasting renunciation is therefore extremely unlikely.
